articles.title: Florida Court Dismisses Tampa General Hospital Lawsuit Against Eli Lilly Over 340B Discounts
articles.summary: A Florida court has dismissed Tampa General Hospital's lawsuit against Eli Lilly regarding restrictions on 340B drug pricing discounts for contract pharmacies. This ruling impacts the ongoing legal battle between pharmaceutical manufacturers and safety-net hospitals over supply chain pricing. For self-funded employers and PBMs, these 340B disputes influence broader drug cost dynamics and manufacturer pricing strategies within the commercial market.
articles.source_line: Source: Fierce Healthcare; Fri, 20 Nov 2026 00:23:07 GMT

articles.title: Ten Emerging Health Benefits Legislative Trends Impacting Self-Funded Employers
articles.summary: A new analysis highlights pending health benefits legislation that self-funded employers must monitor to maintain compliance and manage rising plan costs. These upcoming policy changes directly impact employer-sponsored plan design, fiduciary responsibilities, and pharmacy benefit management strategies. Navigating these regulatory shifts will be crucial for maintaining cost control in employer health plans.

articles.title: Optum Rx Launches New Pharmacy Transparency Tools for Employers
articles.summary: Optum Rx has introduced a suite of new pharmacy tools designed to provide greater pricing visibility and cost management for health plans. This launch reflects ongoing market pressure for PBM transparency that directly impacts self-funded employer benefit strategies. RxBenefits must monitor these industry shifts as competitors roll out new transparency features for plan sponsors.
articles.source_line: Source: Word & Brown General Agency; Thu, 19 Nov 2026 20:59:21 GMT

articles.title: Market Forces Prevent Employers From Securing Optimal Benefits Solutions
articles.summary: An independent benefits platform leader argues that current market dynamics hinder self-funded employers from achieving the best health plan solutions. This critique of industry structures directly impacts how employer health plans evaluate benefits strategies and navigate PBM relationships.
articles.source_line: Source: MedCity News; Thu, 19 Nov 2026 22:45:18 GMT

articles.title: Employer Health Care Costs Projected to Rise at Fastest Rate in Decades
articles.summary: Employer-sponsored health plan costs are surging at their fastest pace in twenty years, placing immense financial pressure on self-funded organizations. Pharmacy benefits, driven largely by specialty drugs and GLP-1 adoption, represent a primary driver of these escalating expenses. Self-funded employers must urgently reevaluate their plan designs and PBM partnerships to contain these unprecedented increases.

articles.title: High-Cost Claimants Drive 40% of Plan Costs, Aon Finds
articles.summary: A new analysis by Aon reveals that just one percent of health plan members account for 40% of total plan costs, underscoring the extreme concentration of healthcare and specialty drug spending. For self-funded employers, this data highlights the critical need for advanced utilization management, aggressive specialty drug containment, and robust stop-loss strategies. Understanding this cost concentration is essential for PBMs and plan sponsors designing targeted interventions for high-need, high-cost conditions.
articles.source_line: Source: Insurance Business; Thu, 19 Nov 2026 14:18:51 GMT

articles.title: Employers Scaling Back GLP-1 Coverage Create Benefits Strategy Challenges
articles.summary: A growing number of self-funded employers are dropping or restricting weight-loss coverage for GLP-1 medications due to mounting cost pressures, leaving employees scrambling for alternatives. This trend highlights the ongoing friction between managing runaway specialty drug spend and maintaining competitive, attractive health plan benefits. For PBMs and employers, it underscores the need for alternative formulary management and utilization controls for anti-obesity medications.
articles.source_line: Source: NBC News; Thu, 19 Nov 2026 10:45:40 GMT

articles.title: Biosimilars Lag in Expanding Earlier Biologic Utilization
articles.summary: Recent analysis highlights that biosimilars are failing to drive earlier utilization of biologic therapies among patients. For self-funded employers and PBMs, this indicates a missed opportunity to leverage lower-cost alternatives to improve both clinical outcomes and specialty drug cost management.
articles.source_line: Source: Center for Biosimilars; Thu, 19 Nov 2026 16:35:05 GMT

articles.title: Judge Dismisses Tampa General Hospital 340B Lawsuit Against Eli Lilly
articles.summary: A federal judge has dismissed Tampa General Hospital's lawsuit challenging drug manufacturer Eli Lilly's restrictions on 340B contract pharmacy pricing. The ruling is a significant development in the ongoing legal battles over 340B drug distribution, which impacts drug pricing dynamics and manufacturer restrictions that ultimately affect commercial health plans and self-funded employer costs.
articles.source_line: Source: Modern Healthcare; Thu, 19 Nov 2026 22:55:33 GMT

articles.title: GLP-1 Spending Threatens Broader Care Management Investments for Employers
articles.summary: Rising expenditures on GLP-1 weight-loss and diabetes drugs are consuming a disproportionate share of employer health plan budgets, frequently overshadowing and defunding broader chronic care management initiatives. For self-funded employers, this dynamic complicates benefit strategy by forcing trade-offs between high-cost specialty pharmacy coverage and holistic health management programs. The key implication is that plan sponsors must reevaluate how they balance pharmacy and medical benefit management to preserve long-term health outcomes.
articles.source_line: Source: MedCity News; Thu, 19 Nov 2026 14:39:27 GMT
